RagShortTexts: Milan’s fields and workshops supported food, equipment and communal defense.

Variants.Content: Fields, roads and channels around Milan supported grain and fodder supplies, while metalworkers made and repaired mail, helmets and weapons. Workshops bought iron and fuel for orders, with payment shaping workers’ income. The commune and rival families sought support, and political conflict affected transport, commissions and defense.

A Milanese smith depends on sound iron, fuel, tools and repeated work at the hearth. In 1259 armour making centres on the equipment of the period, including mail, helmets and reinforcing pieces. The articulated full plate harness of a later age must not be placed on every workshop bench. Fit and repair matter even when a patron pays for elaborate decoration.

Going into battle in Milanese mail gives a soldier real confidence, because the links are close and the plates sit well on the body. Heavy crossbow quarrels glance off the cold-worked iron. Armour does not save a man who breaks ranks, though, so keep your shield up and your place in the line.
